atoms.title: The War of the Worlds 1938 Radio Panic

atoms.text: In the 1930s, one of the main types of entertainment was listening to the radio. Back then, TVs and computers didn’t exist yet. After dinner, families would gather around radios and listen to programmes. At the time, radios were quite large and would often be in the middle of the room. There would be many types of stories, and often they would have episodes, similar to how we watch TV programmes today.

On October 30, 1938, there was a mass panic because of one of these radio programmes. Orson Wells and a group of actors did a radio play based on the book War of the Worlds by H. G. Wells. This book is about aliens attacking the Earth. Many people turned on the radio and thought the reports of alien attacks were real. The main problem was that many people tuned in late and did not hear the introduction explaining it was a story and not real. Some people panicked, called police stations and hid in their basements. Thankfully, not everyone who heard the programme thought it was real, but it shows how strong our imaginations can be.
